item.title: An scp draft for a shower curtain (Need crits!): Re: An scp draft for a shower curtain (Need crits!)
item.content:encoded:
noting a PM request to take another look

[+] Overall
[-] Overall

The quality of the english within this is still subpar. I have attempted to note as much as I can but it is extremely plausible that I have missed a lot and you're likely going to have to try and refine it more yourself, or get additional help.

The actual narrative arc here is…eh. There's a theoretically interesting story of the SCP taking someone over, secretly gaining access to the facility, causing a containment breach and like doing stuff but this doesn't execute it well at all. There are, depending on whether you count the two incident addenda as introduction to this story or not (which I personally wouldn't since it's not clear that they're introducing this story until after it happens) about 800-1100 words before this story even begins, which is not ideal.

Then, a lot of the story just feels very…generic or elided: there's an interview log that doesn't really do anything new with the concept or introduce the characters really or even convey new information so it just feels very much like it's there; and then it's followed by a short record of the foundation trying to terminate this thing that's just kinda there; and then it's followed by a bunch of stuff after the story ends that kinda hints at stuff happening but not in much depth and it feels…underwhelming? Or, rather, it feels like all the interesting stuff happens either between the two interviews or after the second interview and none of it is shown to a reader.

Like, the SCP causes a containment breach for unclear reasons: presumably to escape? But it's not really clear what it's trying to do beyond a generic 'return to where it came from' so it's very whatever. And then it's recaptured…somehow? Like it's grand plan comes crashing down but we never see any part of the plan or how it was foiled so it's like whatever.

This really needs focus: at the end of the day, what do you expect a reader to get out of this? What's the core running story throughout it? And, in turn, how can you bring that story into focus and give it the words it needs to work?

If I was to be extremely honest: I would take this back to the conceptual stage and try and get some reviewers to help you pace this story. Figure out what the beginning, middle and end are, figure out how you can get a reader through the key plot points; figure out how you can evoke the dread that this feels like it's meant to in a reader.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

SCP-XXXX is to be tied up with any sort of bonded material such as fiber or elastic rope when not in an examination, as to restrict possible movement when removed for examination and provide ease of access to SCP-XXXX.

Uh this feels like you've added a bunch of stuff whilst editing and then forgotten to remove the end of the sentence?

'tied up' feels very casual here too and I'm really not sure what the best way around it is other than cutting this whole section and letting the box handle the containment?

Research and inspection checks are to be made when SCP-XXXX consumes enough matter to increase or exceed above its average size

'increase or exceed above its average size' is needlessly confusing: 'grow above its average size' might be clearer though it feels like this should be tied to a fixed size rather than an average since 'average' implies natural variation.

or when recent developments into SCP-XXXX have been discovered.

'developments' and 'discovered' together here feels really awkward: 'made' would be better than 'discovered' I think but it also feels like it needs specificity about what the developments are in

SCP-XXXX should never be removed from its containment for any other reason than testing or research purposes.

would read better with 'other' after 'reason'

until SCP-XXXX is starved enough, wherethat re-containment inside SCP-XXXX’s box is possible

If SCP-XXXX comes into contact with skin or any exposed part of the body; the person in question who has made initial contact with SCP-XXXX is to be marked as SCP-XXXX-A.

The flow of this is wrong: you have to explain what happens with someone who makes contact with the SCP before you can say why they are given a SCP designation.

This kinda implies that the anomaly is marking them as -A or that it's in some way tied into their identity as a result of the anomaly; when really it's the foundation designating them as a sub-anomaly because of the anomalous stuff which happens to them.

The appendage or limb that’s attached to SCP-XXXX is to be amputated immediately, as to avoid the further feeding and development of SCP-XXXX.

Consider:

The appendage attached to SCP-XXXX is to be amputated immediately to prevent further development of SCP-XXXX.

I'm not a fan of 'development' here but I'm not sure what's better: perhaps 'adaption by SCP-XXXX' or something longer that actually covers what change happens?

then an immediate termination of SCP-XXXX-A is put into effect. Alongside the salvaging and cremation of any leftover body parts stuck to SCP-XXXX.

Consider:

then SCP-XXXX-A is to be terminated immediately, followed by the salvage and cremation of any appendages attached to SCP-XXXX.

Issues this is fixing:

  • weird sentence fragment ("Alongside…"
  • 'stuck' feeling really casual
  • just a real clunky way to say they are terminated.

the following anomalies' effects will begin to take place.

'anomalous', not "anomalies'"

SCP-XXX-A’s skin, blood, flesh, and veins will begin to deteriorate into the curtain discarding only bones.

'leaving' would be clearer than 'discarding'; and 'transform' or 'become part of'

This will rapidly lead to blood loss shortly after.

this feels odd because like you just said that the blood gets transformed too so like…it feels on the one hand like the natural conclusion and on the other, like it's technically not actually blood loss in the conventional sense.

If enough human matter equal to SCP-XXXX’s current size and weight is consumed within a recorded one to two day period

I recommended you cut enough last time and I still recommend that:having both 'enough' and 'equal to' is super janky since they're both referring to the quantity and they aren't synonymous.

I'd also cut 'recorded' here: the effects happen even if no-one is paying attention to record them.

from SCP-XXXX that includes: hair, multiple sets of eyes, legs

'includes' should be 'include'

SCP-XXXX has noted to adapted to the situation it is currently faced with when consuming matter.

stuff like 'noted to' isn't really necessary: you can just say what it does, not what people say it does

When in this state due to the adaptation of SCP-XXXX's body, it has been noted that any of the five human senses can be enhanced.

Uh basically large parts of this sentence are just….extraneous? All it's really saying is it can enhance it's senses and so that's all you need to say.

Also humans have, depending on how you count, between 9 and 21 senses: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sense#General so it's probably best to just not specify the number.

Signs of SCP-XXXX first came to light when reports that an unknown shapeless entity had plummeted from the sky, right before the reported deaths of 225 people in Champagne Illinois on 7/27/2005 (Stated below).

'first came to light' feels weirdly casual here. You should also have a comma between 'Champagne' and 'Illinois'. I….generally don't like this. It should be part of the discovery section but it also feels…kinda dumb that it came from space? I feel like it'd be more effective if it opened with the town going silent.

Due to three days of silence from 7/27/2005 - 7/30/2005, 225 reports of civilian deaths were noted by Champagne Illinois requesting military and police aid from the government, following the sighting of SCP-XXXX.

three days of silence doesn't smoothly flow into reports of civilian deaths: this needs some kinda intermediary thing where someone is sent to investigate and discovers them.

The requesting also doesn't flow because there's no-one mentioned who requests this or indication of there actually being a sighting of SCP-XXXX. This sentence is trying to do too much in too few words.

As an immediate response to this unusual jump and spike of numbers, the foundation took interest and shut out every entrance into this town.

What 'unusual jump and spike of numbers'? This should directly reference the reports, not vaguely refer to them.

A priority was set that no one enters or leaves the surrounding area.

this isn't a "priority". Consider: "The surrounding area was locked down" or "The Foundation locked the town down to prevent anyone entering or leaving."

SCP-XXXX was noted in the phase of growth and developing in the husk of a middle-aged man who still hasn’t been identified as of yet when recovered.

another needless used of noted.

'as of yet when recovered' mixes two times together in a confusing way; I'd move 'when recovered' to the start maybe though it feels like the recovery is being elided in an unsatisfying way here.

SCP-XXXX was seen using this husk as a way to disguise and move around the town freely consuming matter, equivalent enough to produce limbs and perform its anomaly’s abilities.

'equivalent enough' is super janky and everything after it feels tacked on.

Commander Linwood ruled nothing could be done beyond the starvation of SCP-XXXX.

Why? At this point, it's almost certainly unclear that starving SCP-XXXX does anything.

and tipping its containment box that it was stored in over at random periods.

why isn't the box heavy enough to prevent this or w/e? This feels like a bad containment procedure, particularly since there's ways to stop a box moving without attaching bolts (bolts are bad since they add holes from the outside to the inside of the box)

After two confirmed weeks of continued testing,

"confirmed" is unnecessary here

SCP-XXXX was reportedly able to jump out and wrap itself around one of the researchers examining SCP-XXXX.

"reportedly" adds unnecessary uncertainty about what happened here: either it did do this or it didn't but it can't be both.

This resulted in the researcher panicking and frantically rip SCP-XXXX off of them, but the suit was torn in the process

'ripped' would be more grammatically correct.

"the suit" is unclear here because like…who's suit is it? the researchers? it's mentioned like it's been referred to previously but it hasn't so it feels jarring.

Little matter was consumed in the time it took to contain SCP-XXXX.

What does 'little matter' mean here?

The internal structure of the containment cell was slightly weakened and shortly repaired after the incident.

'but repaired shortly after the incident' would be clearer. Then again, it being damaged and then immediately repaired raises the question of why even bother mentioning this since it's so inconsequential?

Both Dr. Connor and other researchers working with SCP-XXXX have put into question the severity of another containment breach Scp be tied up with any bounded material to ensure SCP-XXXX does not breach containment by force. And to make sure future examinations undergo safely.

Awkward fragment sentence at the end; Dr. Connor is mentioned here like we're meant to know who he is but this is the first mention of it; and everything after 'containment breach' feels like an editing mistake?

From recent research and developments that have been made about SCP-XXXX, it appears that SCP-XXXX does not only retain the form of a shower curtain but; also possess shapeshifting abilities.

This is wack because we aren't shown any of the research or developments that lead to this conclusion.

During a recent on-site breach. (See Addendum Incident-2) SCP-XXXX accumulated enough time to take the shape and form of a researcher assigned to SCP-XXXX.

The first period here is unnecessary.

Also why wasn't this mentioned in the Incident-2 section since it happened then?

SCP-XXXX has expressed several hostile concerns about returning home

What is a 'hostile concern about returning home'?

Also like why are we not shown any of this until the interview? Like I don't see why you're summarising this all here and then immediately launching into an interview that like…reveals this?

And or lacks the nutrients to perform said anomalies effects.

Weird sentence fragment. You do this a lot: if you are starting a sentence with a conjunction like 'and' or 'but', it probably wants to be part of the previous sentence.

Interviewer: Dr. Conner

Every other time, you've spelt this 'Connor'. Either is correct but it should be consistent.

(Dr. Connor is interrupted by SCP-XXXX)

Unnecessary: "founda-" makes it clear Connor was interrupted, and the SCP talking next makes it clear it was by the SCP.

If it will humor you, then I’ll play your little games until I become bored.

this just feels really weird? one moment the SCP is demanding to be released, the next it's being passive

Starvation doesn’t seem to have any effect either, other than keeping it to a containable and safe enough size.

I'd be tempted to cut 'and safe' here too. Also like…why? Surely if starvation is effective at weakening it, applying more starvation will, eventually, kill it?

Following a cataclysmic breach of Site-19. SCP-XXXX was reported to be

these should be the same sentence.

Both Dr. Adam and Dr. Connor’s body were recovered after the incident is declared deceased as of this time.

I believe that 'is' should be 'and'.

[-] Line By Line

item.title: Shepherd boy (working title): Re: Shepherd boy
item.content:encoded:
► my detailed thoughts◄
- close

SCP-XXXX is to be stored in Containment Area M21 located in 300m underground of the Gobi desert in Mongolia.

Delete that second “in” (right before 300m)

SCP-XXXX is to be held in a 5 m cube made of entirely Tungsten metal, with no gap for organic life to enter.

Why does it matter that the cube be Five meters in length/widtch/height? What if it were 4.98 meters? Would that invalidate the containment? This is why specific measurements of containment chambers is mostly avoided these days.

If any entities that reside in SCP-XXXX-1 move from their position, they are to be immediately apprehended and interrogated before being held in a cell with same containment procedure as SCP-CXXX.

Suggest: Entities residing in SCP-XXXX-1 that move from their position, are to be apprehended, interrogated, and remanded to a containment cell under equivalent containment procedures as SCP-XXXX.

No more than five personnel wearing Hazmat suits, are to enter SCP-XXXX-1 at the same time. Its activity is to be monitored 24/7 and no unauthorized personnel and civilian are to be in the proximity of the area or enter SCP-XXXX-1.

Suggest: A maximum of five hazmat protected personnel are permitted to enter SCP-XXXX-1 at any given time. Access to SCP-XXXX-1 is restricted to security cleared personnel.

In the event of a Containment Breach, all on site researchers and personnel are to evacuate immediately or stay in shelter until the MTF Theta-4 (“Gardeners”) arrive at the facility and apprehended the entity.

Suggest: In the event of a containment breach, all on-site personnel are to evacuate or shelter in place until such time as MTF-Theta-4 (“Gardeners”) apprehend the entity.

ALSO: which entity? Clarify

SCP-CXXX consists of two components: a cave (SCP-XXXX-1) and humanoid protecting it (SCP-XXXX).

Suggest: SCP-XXXX consists of two interrelated anomalies: a cave, designated as SCP-XXXX-1 and a humanoid entity guarding the cave, designated as SCP-XXXX.
ALSO: I suggest reversing the designations, the Cave could be the XXXX and the humanoid, -1, because it seems the cave is the central anomaly.

SCP-XXXX is a Hun male, its skin is olive-brown from sunburn and wears an old dark green Hun area deel1 which been ripped and torn, however, SCP-XXXX refused to change it.

SCP-XXXX has the ability to manifest entities made out of natural components which resemble a Chinese dragon. Entities length is unknown.
So several things, “an old dark green Hun area deel” is confusing… suggest: “SCP-XXXX is a Hun male, its skin is olive-brown from sun damage and an deteriorating, dark-green Hun deel that the entity refuses to change.” & I don’t know what “made out of natural components” means in this context, so I would clarify.

ALSO: IS this meant to be two paragraphs? If so, there is no spacing between them.

SCP-XXXX-1 is a cave under abandoned Mining factory, it is measured to be around 6 kilometers deep.

Suggest: a cave under an abandoned mining facility, measured to be approximately six kilometers below the surface.

  • There is no such thing as a mining factory, change this everywhere… it’s a facility or just a mine.

However, how big SCP-XXXX-1 mass is impossible to measure. SCP-XXXX-1 resides a snake-like creature approximately 1 kilometers, maybe even bigger.

Suggest: Exact measurements of SCP-XXXX-1’s dimensions have been impossible due to a large serpentine entity, at least one kilometer in length, that resides within the cave.

About fifty kilometers down, there is a massive field stretching further from the human eye, filled with stationary humanoids varies in ages, they're made out of natural components, different species of flowers but growing in the same root. The radio cuts off the moment entering SCP-XXXX-1.

Fifty kilometers down where? I thought you said the cave was 6 km below the surface? What do you mean? Also this is just really awkwardly written.

The investigation into SCP-XXXX-1 and its relation with SCP-XXXX is ongoing.

Cut this. It’s implied because there’s more to read after it.

This is a critique in progress… You have so many awkward phrases and poorly structured sentences… I would sit down and really examine your work here, and see if you can't clean it up without myself or another critter to do so.

Additionally, all the dialogue is stilted and hard to read. Go through it and say each line aloud, then if it sounds awkward try to make it sound more grounded and believable.

item.title: Go For Gold! - Cars, Corpses, and Consumption!: Re: Go For Gold! - Cars, Corpses, and Consumption!
item.content:encoded:
Don't think of a bank account as something that has a dollar added to it or subtracted from it ad random. Think of it as a record of transactions, or a closed system of exchanges. Money does not come from nowhere - someone has to be depositing money into those accounts from business entity. This might be a neat use case for Envelope Logistics, if that's a direction you want to take it.

Basically, make sure there's some kind of reasonable path for the consumer to get money. Maybe they get diamonds or processed gold in the mail, or winning lottery tickets, etc.

item.title: Try again? Fugitive vs the Yakuza: Re: Try again? Fugitive vs the Yakuza
item.content:encoded:
Requested to review by Wikidot PM.

+ show block
– hide block

"You here to talk to the boss?"

Personally, I feel like this should be its own separate line.

He smiles when you arrive at his desk.

I can't place my finger on it, but this just seems out of flow for the rest of the interaction. You'd think this guy would smile on first seeing him, or as he was lighting the cigarette.

"Thank you." Tsuyaki leans back in his chair, and lights a cigarette.

"So tell me, how did you get this money?" Tsuyaki blows smoke into your face as he talks.

You could probably combine this into one paragraph: "Thank you." Tsuyaki leans back in his chair, and lights a cigarette. He blows smoke into your face as he continues to talk. "So tell me, how did you get this money?"

"Really? Not many people who come to me have 10,000,000 yen. It's even stranger that a foreigner would." Tsuyaki leans forward.

"So tell me. Did you steal this money?"

Same here.

"No, I don't like having a target on my back." Tsuyaki begins to laugh.

"I guess that's why you want me to smuggle you off the island." You remain silent as you wait for your reward.

Yet more weird line breaking. I think it flows better as:

"No, I don't like having a target on my back."

"I guess that's why you want me to smuggle you off the island." Tsuyaki begins to laugh.

You remain silent as you wait for your reward.

"Or are you running from the GOC?"

Probably would combine this with the paragraph above it.

Tsuyaki's eyes dart behind you for a brief moment.

Make this separate from the reader's dialogue. At this point, I think you get my drift. Keep Tsuyaki's actions separate from the reader's dialogue, and vice versa. I'm going to stop pointing it out now.

You simultaneously remove your gun, and shoot the right in the chest.

Did you accidentally a word here?

"I would never help you. Traitors deserve to die." Tsuyaki begins to laugh.

Yeah, this is some Snidely Whiplash levels of villain dialogue here, my dude. I imagine people who just had a gun fired next to their head are not quite cartoony when they speak.

When the three guards rush around the corner, you begin to open fire. one goes down, as the others duck behind cover, and return fire.

Ending two sentences after another with the same word always parses weird to me. Might want to switch up the vocab for one of these two.

The only survivors of the operation was Roach and fellow
strike team members Echo and Blanket. After review of the

Weird line break here.

All in all, it's a bit of a fun ride through the various iterations of these events. Nothing groundbreaking, but a neat bit of noir-style action. That said, when you get to the personnel file on roach you really break all your flow and momentum to a halt. To be honest, that level of exposition kills the story dead. While it is likely going to be essential info for your overall story arc, I'd say it would be better if you capped off the story and including the file in another piece. But that's just my opinion.

item.title: Explained SCP in need of review: Re: Explained SCP in need of review
item.content:encoded:
It's certainly clever, albeit stretching the use of the 'explained SCP' category.

The core idea has merit and the narrative is quite good. The ending works but I'm a bit let down by the actual explanation of what happens (that being "weird eldritch things"). I don't know if that because of a preconceived notion that -EX articles need to be fully explainable or because it feels like a cop out.

I think this article is 85% of the way there, and would be well-served by a purely non-anomalous rationale for Thompson's defection - e.g. bureaucratic reasons.

item.title: Go For Gold! - Cars, Corpses, and Consumption!: Re: Go For Gold! - Cars, Corpses, and Consumption!
item.content:encoded:
I have very mixed feelings about this. The core ideal is fine, but I'm morally obligated to point out that compulsion should be avoided.

The first two logs are good. The third is entirely too wordy and I think breaks the suspension of disbelief - O5 should have more control over itself and realize exactly what is happening - not break down into disorder and infighting.

The description is greatly improved but there's still a massive dangling thread in that 'bank account money' comes out of thin air, which can't really happen with such a computerized banking system we have today. I think there's room for cleverness in handling that can add verisimilitude to what is admittedly a rather wacky article. The asteroid bit is also entirely extraneous and I'm not sure what its purpose is.

The writing is certainly better than the original article, but I think I would still no vote. The logs add a lot but my opinion is soured by the third log. The ending still works as it did in the original article. As a rewrite, I think you're still a bit hamstrung by the original core idea and I'm not sure there's much that can be done to mitigate that without changing the article fundamentally.

item.title: Draft "Disconnected Restroom": Re: Draft "Disconnected Restroom"
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this.

I took a quick look at the draft. There are a lot of simple errors, such as lack of correct paragraph spacing, unnecessary crossed-out materials in the containment (try to avoid redacting or withdrawing anything in that section; if you really must include earlier versions of containment, I recommend having an archived version in a collapsible), and inconsistent section heading capitalization. The containment procedures are rather disorganized as well; try to group similar information together rather than having it all sort of scattered and in need of clear flow/transition between topics.

Address these issues first and let me know when you have done so; I will then provide a full review of the draft.

item.title: Need critiques!: Forum Criticism Team - Moderator Post
item.content:encoded:
Atreum, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.
